content:
Dating reality shows have long been a popular genre, but Apple TV+ has never ventured into this space. Although its newly announced series *The Last Person on Earth* is positioned as a "documentary series" rather than a "reality show," it is still the streaming platform's first dating programme.

*The Last Person on Earth* is hosted by renowned relationship therapist Esther Perel and described as an "innovative experiment".

Esther Perel is a celebrated relationship therapist and *New York Times* bestselling author specialising in the field of human relationships.

Perel is also the central figure in Apple TV+'s newly announced eight-episode dating documentary series *The Last Person on Earth*.

The press release states: "In the show, seemingly mismatched pairs are carefully matched by Perel and a team of matchmakers and therapists, before embarking on a journey to some of the world's most romantic and remote destinations."

It sounds very much like a reality show, but without the negative baggage that the "reality" brand carries. I suspect Apple is trying to create a sense of "elevation" around the dating show format, hence labelling it a "documentary series".

The series has yet to announce a premiere date and is expected to debut in 2027.

Incidentally, Apple also announced yesterday that it will adapt bestselling novelist Rebecca Yarros's latest romance novel into a television series. Clearly, the streaming platform is striving to break out of its existing core genres of sci-fi, comedy and thriller, venturing into new territory.

Apple TV+ costs US$12.99 per month, with discounts available through the Apple One bundle subscription.
